_about: The Models tab of the hangar page (tools/hangar.html): every render Ryan judges, by chassis. A round adds its pictures under docs/hangar/renders/<chassis>/, moves the previous 'images' to 'before' with a summary, and writes 'when' and 'note'; then the page is republished with the new files (tools/hangar_data.py prints the files map). 'classes' is the silhouette classes section, a list of blocks shown in order.

classes.title: Silhouette classes
classes.plate: What a swapped component wears at a gun mount · the rule settled 30 September

blocks.note: Hardpoints are gun mounts. A weapon, or equipment that can look like one (a shield projector, a buff coil), wears its class at the next mount in the die's order, in its own maker's metal; armour panels and vents take a die entry and no mount, since they are applied to the whole machine. Five classes: barrel, twin barrel, rack, blade (katar-style, punching forward) and dish. A machine with more hardpoints than stock guns carries bare mount pads. Shown: a Minerva barrel, a Wainwright & Sutler rack, a Kestrel dish, an Arsenal blade.

Four refits rendered with RIFTGATE_FIT: the Honey Badger with a W&S Lance on the wrist, a Heat Sink (which shows nowhere), an Arsenal Blazethrower on the left pauldron and a Kestrel Deflector's dish on the right; the Clydesdale with an Arc Projector in place of the Lance and, on its bare mounts, a Missile Rack, Soulcutter Talons and an Overcharge Coil; the Sparrowhawk with Soulcutter Talons as a wing blade and Meteor Artillery on the other tip; the Wild Boar with a Plasma Carbine and a Blazethrower on its rear quarters.

badger.note: The Bullion Fragmenter's bore inset so it reads hollow (Ryan): a pale sawn rim at the muzzle, the bore lined dark five units in with a dark floor. The breech block, its hazard band and the crusher hopper as the second pass. Ryan called it good the same day.

before.summary: Before: twelfth round, second pass, 6 October (the sawed-off cannon with a flat bore)

clydesdale.note: The shins stand plumb, each hoof under its knee, the knee three forward of the hip, so only the thigh angles (Ryan: the stance leaned too far forward; a straight leg, a straight calf or less of a lean). It gallops, pushed toward a lumbering giant (the sixteenth notes): barely airborne, the hull rocking and sinking onto every hoof; the trot is an option on the hangar's Walk.

before.summary: Before: the eleventh notes, 6 October (the knee four forward, the shin raking back to a hoof under the hip)

sparrowhawk.note: The wings' roots sit inside the fuselage at their leading edge (Ryan: not sure its wings meet the front of the fuselage; they stood just proud of it, by under a unit, where the fuselage narrows). The exhausts' fitted glow as before.

before.summary: Before: the fourth acts pass, 5 October (the wing roots just proud of the fuselage at the front)

armadillo.when: The sixth notes, 5 October; a come-about on planted footwork, 20 October.
armadillo.note: A square channel cut through the shell along the missile cell's own line, so the cell slides up out of it instead of through the top panel; the stripe frame a sleeve over its lower part, floored dark deep in the shell. The third picture is still the fourteenth round's, with a Slug Cannon and a Missile Rack fitted to the forward ports. Ryan, 20 October: with no head and no waist it turns its whole shell to look, in the diagonal pairs it walks in, eight degrees on the planted pair a step, twenty-four round, guns up and lamps lit while it holds, then back (come_about; every hip's own yaw and roll keep its foot planted and pointing where it landed). Judge it running in the Animation tab.

images.alt: armadillo, coming about, a pair stepping

before.summary: Before: the fifth notes, 5 October (the cell's frame sitting on the shell)

prairie_dog.note: The front arches and the aprons trimmed to the hood (Ryan: minimise the fronts' overlap with it): each front arch's inner edge now follows the hood's own edge a quarter of a unit inside it, with a section at the hood's kink so it follows the taper, where it had run a unit to a unit and a half over the hood on one straight line; the aprons stop a quarter of a unit inside the body's flank, not a whole unit. The arches' depth, a whole unit lower, and the rev at five degrees as Ryan settled them; the livery aprons, the axle covers and the wheels as before.

before.summary: Before: 9 October, fifth pass (the front arches and aprons reaching a unit or more over the hood)

goshawk.note: The cannon's lights banked down at rest (a new ember tile, the glow at under a third of its light) so its charge burns far hotter against them; the spine stays lit through the whole charge. At rest the vents and the bore read dark red.

before.summary: Before: the fifth notes, 5 October (the cannon's lights at the full glow at rest)

nemesis.when: Sixth round, 1 October; a square-up and a braced meteor stance on planted footwork, 20 October.
nemesis.note: The condenser's slots on the lit tile too. Otherwise as the fifth round. Ryan, 20 October (lateral motion for an angry boy): it squares up to something at its left, the left foot stamping out wide and back as the whole machine turns on its planted right and drops into the stance, the fists up, the torso leaning in and wound a little further, the core burning while it glares, then the stamp back (square_up; a sideways pace was built first and looked like dancing); and the meteor's firing stance is a real one, the right foot back and out as the whole machine turns ten degrees to its mark on its planted left, the waist's turn on top (raise_meteor). Judge them running in the Animation tab.

images.alt: nemesis, squared up, the left foot stamped out

ammit.when: The fifth notes, 5 October; a circling act on planted footwork, 20 October.
ammit.note: Wrists on the middle hands, so the talons stay flat on the ground as it sinks, threatens and walks, and the front toes splayed a little (Ryan, 5 October). A waist under the upper body, so it turns without pivoting on its feet. Ryan, 20 October (lateral motion for a creepy stalker): it circles its prey with the snout kept on it, the body sliding round an arc about a point ahead and turning to face it, the feet and the hands scuttling sideways under it, the hands two short steps to a foot's one, two moves round to one side, a pause, and two back (one each way through the centre came first; Ryan: two and back is more effective), nose down, the claws at their guard with the talons slowly working (circle). Judge it running in the Animation tab.

images.alt: ammit, circling its prey, a hand and a foot stepping

stingray.note: The starboard lift fan's blades mirrored (Ryan: its pitch was the port fan's while it spins the other way), so each rotor's blades lead with their raised edge as it turns. The third picture is from straight behind and above.

before.summary: Before: the tenth pass, 5 October (both rotors' blades pitched the same way)

puffin.when: The swap, the amplify lit for real, 28 October.
puffin.note: Ryan's swap (26 October: the Storm Petrel's first cut, a speedboat with a mast, reads as a research boat, which is the Puffin): the long chined boat at the light size, the skirt bow to stern, the hull thicker amidships with its bottom rising to the prow and the stern (his notes of the 27th), the Ionizer's dish down on its mast's yoke, the side plates hinged low at the chine and level under way as repulsors (their undersides carrying the lit discs), folding up in a fight as shield amplifiers (the last picture, the amplify act), one booster drawn in over the afterdeck. Ryan's notes on the landing (28 October): the plates fold nearer plumb, and the amplify lights a rim round each plate's edge with the strips, the bosses, the discs underneath and the nozzles, hot. His second notes (no glow seen; the forward disc stuck out of the plate's edge; the discs should glow): the amplify's lights had been named by a prefix the rig never matches, so nothing lit; named whole now, the rims, the strips, the bosses, the discs and the nozzles all blaze (the last picture), the build refuses a glow that labels no part, and the forward disc sits inside the plate's outline.

images.alt: puffin, the plates folded up to amplify

before.summary: Before: the eighth pass, 5 October (the wide low hull on two giant boosters, the base the Storm Petrel took).

images.alt: puffin, before, from behind and above

funnel_web.when: Fourth cut, 19 October; revised on Ryan's fifth to eleventh notes, 19 and 20 October, and good to go on the eleventh.
funnel_web.note: Ryan's fourth notes (19 October): the body in W&S's military camp, the Prairie Dog's and the gunship's, not the Clydesdale's and the Dingo's funky steam, more aggressive; the side guns pitch only, the torso twist aims them; nothing hanging like a proboscis; the upper legs in the walk beside the solver, the Ammit's way, so it walks creepy. His fifth: the fore feet's two short steps hot-stepped, far too busy, and the head's turn looked weird, both cut, the feet kept down; the body is great; two static forward guns instead of the single centred one, the jaw reworked for them, one mount left on top, and the web launcher one of the side guns. As it stands: a dark lower hull running into a wide flat jaw under an armoured upper hull with a wedge brow, two slit eyes in a dark visor band, livery appliqué on the flanks, an exhaust grille and a whip antenna at the tail; the Maxigun and the Twin Autoguns static in the jaw's two mantlets, the Howitzer alone on the roof on its elevation, the web launcher's four tubes out of the left pod on its elevation, the dish on the right pod. The creep: every foot one step a stride, out of step, and the coxae rowing (his sixth notes, his pick of the options: the feet had flicked forward): each leg's base swings forward as its foot lands, back through the stance and forward through the swing, the solver planting the foot under it, so the whole leg sweeps as one; the stride lengthened and the foot's carry widened, so the swing is slower with the feet still down seven tenths of the time. His seventh: the walk does not look too bad; the bow guns pulled back in, the jaw shorter and the mantlets near flush; the roof mount moved aft of the pods; and the row at its extreme to see, twenty degrees, the Walk's option row_extreme in the Animation tab. His eighth: the two rows told apart by nobody, so the extreme option is gone; the roof mount sunk into the roof (a gap showed); the flank plates embraced as raked fins in the livery, rising up and behind, a little flair on a utilitarian maker; the guns clipped the fore legs in the scan and the sighting, so a twist is now the head's twenty degrees and a shuffle of the legs for the rest, a little predatory skittering; and the vertical range this walker alone has, its legs and its torso mount looking up and down, so it rears, sinks and coils through the acts. His ninth (20 October): the fins good, their base to be squared off; the antenna floated, its base now runs into the hull; and the shuffle slid since the feet were not planted, so each leg has a yaw joint at its root and a pivot solver keeps every foot not stepping planted while the body turns. His tenth, the same day: a toned-back cut of the fins came out too small, so they are the eighth's shape and size again on a level base sunk in the bracket; and the scan's first turn, the slow one, now goes in under a second. His eleventh, the same day: the antenna a little inboard, clear of the fin, and the model is good to go. Rendered bare; the coil of its stalk and a side-on moment of the creep beside the front and rear. Judge the acts and the walk running in the Animation tab.

images.alt: funnel-web, coiled low in its stalk
funnel-web, a moment of the creep, side on

skua.when: Second round, the jaeger; its acts the Kite's size, 28 October (the run a dive).
skua.note: Ryan's pick from five rounds of looks (23 to 27 October, docs/looks/kestrel_skua*.png): the jaeger, the seabird's wings as the swing. A short deep fuselage into one booster, a jet's straight nose with the bird's dark cap (his last note: the bent tip at the nose ditched), the fixed arms flat from low on the flank to a wrist drum and the long hands swinging from it, the white flash across their roots, a V tail, two streamers, the fin carried back over the booster and tall, the Flechette Pod twin pods on the spine. The last picture is the strafing run, the hands swept. Ryan's notes on the landing (28 October: the strafing run and the sweep-dash read the same; it wants the Kite's treatment, bigger animations): five acts like the Kite's, the strafing run rolling in and diving hard with the pods firing at the bottom, the Kite's barrel roll with the hands swept, the stoops wider and rolled far over, the Kite's loop on the map only, and the flare nose-high with the hands rocking. The last picture is the strafing run's dive. His second notes the same day (the run "just kind of wiggles"; the wings stay extended for a barrel roll): the strafing run now climbs back and up off its hex, wings over with the hands sweeping back, dives steeply on its foe with the pods firing twice at the bottom, and climbs away rolled over with the hands spreading to brake; the barrel roll flies with the hands spread. The last picture is the run's bottom. His third notes, from the phone (the run read as bobbing and swaying, never leaving its hex; the five acts and the wings-out roll confirmed): the run and the stoops at the Kite's loop's scale, the run climbing a hex back and high, diving through its hex a full hex on and arcing back over the top, the stoops a hex wide each way.

before.summary: Before: the first cut, 23 October (the conventional swing-wing jet, Ryan: an F-14 poly for poly).

images.alt: skua, before, the strafing run, wings swept

needletail.note: Claude's first cut, 23 October (Ryan: models for every chassis ready to build, their silhouettes apart from the Kestrel roster's). From above, the view the player reads, the roster is the Kite's dart on forward-swept wings with a V tail, the Buzzard's tailless plank, the Puffin's blunt hull on stubs, and the Lammergeier's two wing pairs to come. The Needletail is a needle of a fuselage on a short straight stub wing with a big booster nacelle on each tip, standing upright at rest so it hovers on them, exhausts down, where the Buzzard's nacelles tilt on the shoulders of a broad-winged airframe; a long thin tail ending in a dark needle with an X of small fins; a wide spotter's canopy; the Fovea Designator a sensor ball on a mast behind it, turning and nodding, its lens lit as it paints. Its acts: the transition to level flight and back, a sidestep, designating, backpedalling on its nacelles tipped back. On the move its nacelles tilt level as it gathers speed and come upright as it slows. Ryan's to judge running.

storm_petrel.when: The swap, the field lit, the arch sleeved, 28 October.
storm_petrel.note: Ryan's swap: the Puffin's wide hull with the two giant boosters, at the medium size, for the shield off-tank; his notes of the 27th ("great"): the nose snubbed so the port doubled, the louvred vent housings back on the booster covers and vents on the prow's top and flanks. No plate: the Riot Field is the four emitter pylons on the cheeks, the lit rails along their creases and the arch over the canopy; St. Elmo's fire is the open port in the nose, a chine-shaped mouth with the corona inside (the last picture, the st_elmo act). Ryan's notes on the landing (28 October: more lit areas, much brighter when lit; the corona a white block whose act showed nothing; more livery): lit strips along the flanks and caps on the fin tips join the rails, the emitters and the arch, all far hotter when the field is up; St. Elmo's fire is a small core deep in the mouth with eight sparks round the lip and a ring inside it, dim at rest, that crackle white one after another as the hull heaves and shudders; a cobalt chine stripe, a prow panel, booster bands and the emitter pylons in the livery. His second notes: the emitter pylon ahead of each tub was a livery chunk in the way of the mount, so the emitters stand clear ahead of the muzzle and behind the breech, low and in the hull's colour; the arch's glow ran along its underside, hidden, so the arch is now a thin lit line under eight sleeves of plate with the light showing between them; the booster bands lie flush as paint. His third: the sleeves longer, covering most of the band. His fourth: the sleeves about two thirds of each span, and the arch on feet that stand on the deck (it floated).

images.alt: storm_petrel, St. Elmo's fire in the port

before.summary: Before: the first cut, 23 October (the long narrow hull under two raised riot plates and a mast, the base the Puffin took).

giant_petrel.note: Claude's first cut, 23 October (Ryan: models for every chassis ready to build, their silhouettes apart from the Kestrel roster's). From above, the view the player reads, the roster is the Kite's dart on forward-swept wings with a V tail, the Buzzard's tailless plank, the Puffin's blunt hull on stubs, and the Lammergeier's two wing pairs to come. The Giant Petrel is after the Lun: a long flying-boat hull, the longest thing Kestrel builds; eight boosters in two banks of four on canards over the bow (the Immelmann Booster), pitching to blow under the wings; short cobalt wings low on the hull with float pontoons and endplates; a tall T-tail; the Spindrift Salvo's three pairs of tubes along the spine on a plinth that elevates, each back-blast lit; the Reheat Uplink's dish behind the cockpit; two turrets. Its acts: the salvo, the Immelmann, the uplink, a traverse. On the move it runs heavy and slow, nose a touch up. Ryan's to judge running.

images.alt: giant petrel, the salvo, its battery raised

lammergeier.when: First model, the flying wing, the launcher nacelles on the skin, 28 October.
lammergeier.note: The chrome chevron drawn as a hovercraft for the Giant Petrel (the third round, docs/looks/kestrel_giant.png), given to the Lammergeier airborne on Ryan's thought of 27 October ("looks good but careful on the weapon mount placement so they don't clip"): a deeper centre body with the canopy forward and the bomb bay under it on a lit seam, four booster drums across the trailing edge, the Syrinx Drone's tubes in the leading edge's roots, the Lorentz Contractor's dish on a dorsal pylon, the mounts on the wing in the bays between the drums. The last picture is the lay_mines act. 28 October: the drone tubes sit in a pod on each leading-edge root, its face raked with the edge, so the wing's skin no longer shows inside them (Ryan's note). His second notes (the pods did not work as meant): each is now a nacelle on the leading-edge root that carries the wing's full thickness forward to a blunt raked face, top and bottom, the two tubes let into the face. His third (the box was fine; the hull-coloured tube ends clipping through its raked face were the mistake): each tube's mouth follows the face's rake, a touch proud of it, in the nacelle's dark. His fourth: the tubes bored twelve deep (an end cap is no tube). His fifth (the mouths read as end caps, not inset): each mouth is a hole cut through the face plate, the bore flush in it in the lighter plate so its far wall catches the light. His sixth (the open bores showed the wing's skin again, which the caps had hidden: the skin climbs over the bore's depth): the nacelle rides on the wing's upper skin, its underside following the skin's rise from the edge, the tubes above the skin the whole way.
